beats.text: A thirty-sheet bid set arrives. Keep the floor plan and the two mechanical sheets.
Name the working sheet: A-101 · First Floor Plan.
Open sheet A-101, the office suite's floor plan.
Check the scale against a printed dimension before counting anything.
Draw a box over each room. The app reads its name off the plan and works out the air it needs.
Set up the rooftop unit: RTU-1, 3,000 CFM, 0.8 inches of static pressure.
Place the unit on the roof, over the corridor.
Create a supply diffuser rated at 150 CFM.
Three diffusers are not enough air for this room.
The fourth meets the room's airflow, and its tag turns green.
Place diffusers in every other room.
Trace the main supply duct, starting at the unit.
Press S to step the duct size down after each branch takes its air.
Run a branch duct into each room. The app counts each tap fitting.
For the last branch, the app suggests the size from the room's airflow.
Add the return air: two grilles and a return duct back to the unit.
Place the thermostat.
Add an exhaust fan, EF-1, with a grille in each restroom.
Open the duct schedule: every duct size with its metal gauge and weight.
Fittings are counted from the drawing. Flexible duct is listed per diffuser.
The total sheet-metal weight to bid.
The bid check confirms every room gets its air and the unit has the capacity.
It checks the unit's fan can push air down the longest duct path.
Tick off the thermostat location as confirmed.
Hide the marks, then show them again, to check the floor for anything missed.
Copy the duct schedule into the pricing app.
